title: Tailoring for MetaHumans: CLO and Marvelous Designer to Unreal Engine Live Demo
content:
# ![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202604/18b5b426d8be42da832d12cffec2dfa4/images/32b098532044470bbd0ac615a200c540CONNECT%20MetaHuman%20Thumbnail.png)**Tailoring for MetaHumans Live Demo + Q &A**

We all love the built-in CLO and Marvelous Designer avatars, but what if you’re looking for something a bit more customizable? That’s where our friends at Epic Games can help. We recently teamed up with the [_MetaHuman_](https://www.metahuman.com/)and [_Unreal Engine_](https://www.unrealengine.com/) teams for a webinar exploring the full workflow—from creating a MetaHuman, importing it into CLO or Marvelous Designer, and bringing it all into Unreal Engine for use in your projects. Check out the full recording for a step-by-step demonstration of the process.

YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=s1aP1kFyvKk?start=0

# **Learn more about creating garments for MetaHumans**

Looking to learn more? We put together some resources to help you in your CLO to Unreal journey. Find out more about CLO, Marvelous Designer, MetaHuman, Unreal Engine, and the way they all work together!

# **MetaHuman resources**

[ _Creating Parametric Clothing for Fab  
  
_](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/unreal-engine/creating-parametric-clothing-for-fab)This step-by-step outline showcases the process of creating parametric (resizable) clothing assets for MetaHumans.  
  
[ _MetaHuman Conform Topology_](https://www.fab.com/listings/98f7b49d-f5dc-45c4-b590-52dbb4f951c0)

Download this free set of asset files to make custom characters you’ve sculpted fully compatible with the MetaHuman system.  


# **CLO and Marvelous Designer resources**

[ _CLO Quick Start_](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VCKS0qEOJk0)

This step-by-step tutorial series will walk you through everything you need to kickstart your CLO journey.

[_Pattern Drafter_](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4Ubv8p8qTnE&t=2291s)

This mini workshop demonstrates the steps to reverse-engineer a garment pattern using the Pattern Drafter.

[_3D Pen_](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mSJLFcYUSTY&t=734s)

Learn about the updated 3D Pen that enables you to draw garment silhouettes around the avatar directly from the 3D space and instantly convert them into 2D patterns.

[_Style Line Tools_](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QDaAGBd_Oc4&t=164s)

Watch this video to explore how to use the style line tools in CLO, also applicable to Marvelous Designer.__

[_Marvelous Designer Quick Start_](https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLYQUdblF9eDXA3R44hr-wcr2lErnoU1_3)

New to Marvelous Designer? This quick start guide will walk you through the basics of the software.

# **Integrating CLO and Marvelous Designer with Unreal Engine**

Build out your garment design, simulation, and animation pipeline with these useful resources on combining the power of CLO and Marvelous Designer with Unreal Engine.  
  
[_CLO to MetaHuman: USD Garment Integration Workflow_](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/53322960594969-CLO-to-MetaHuman-USD-Garment-Integration-Workflow)

This guide outlines the entire workflow for exporting garments from Marvelous Designer as USD and integrating them with MetaHuman.

[_Marvelous Designer to MetaHuman: USD Garment Integration Workflow_](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/en-us/articles/52699135975705-Marvelous-Designer-to-MetaHuman-USD-Garment-Integration-Workflow)

This guide outlines the workflow for exporting garments from Marvelous Designer as USD and integrating them with MetaHuman.

[_Marvelous Designer 2025.2: How to Import MetaHumans in DNA as Avatars_](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=t3GATippRqY)

This short tutorial walks you through the process of importing a MetaHuman in DNA format to Marvelous Designer for use as an avatar.  
  
[_CLO/MD LiveSync manual_](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/en-us/categories/44704952678809-LiveSync)

Get set up with LiveSync—a bridge that connects CLO and Unreal Editor (CLO LiveSync), or Marvelous Designer and Unreal Editor (MD LiveSync), with the aim of shortening workflows between these tools and Unreal Engine.

[_Matt Workman’s Unreal Engine x Marvelous Designer tutorial_](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CoYfZP5GEJM)

Learn how to send an animated MetaHuman from Unreal Engine 5.6 to Marvelous Designer, create and simulate clothing, and send the simulated garments back to Unreal Engine using the CLO / Marvelous Designer LiveSync 2 plugin.

[_My Exact CLO3D to Unreal Engine 5.7 Workflow_](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3Cp2ngrgEHo)

Discover how to move your CLO assets into Unreal Engine in this beginners’ tutorial by aschno. She covers everything from installation and plugins to UI navigation, target lighting, MetaHuman import, and CLO LiveSync integration.

# **Using your assets in Unreal Engine**

Once you’ve decked out your MetaHuman in their new clothes, you can use Unreal Engine’s Chaos Cloth system to bring realistic cloth movement that responds to character motion, gravity, and wind.

  
[_Chaos Cloth Demystified: A Practical Guide for Artists  
_](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IzmJnTnphBc)In this session recorded at Unreal Fest Orlando 2025, we unlock the full potential of Chaos Cloth with an artist-friendly guide to creating a robust production-ready pipeline.  
  
[_Official documentation by Tim Brakensiek_](https://dev.epicgames.com/community/profile/Gk/gozerKeymaster)

Epic’s Tim Brakensiek has put together a number of tutorial videos that explore different Chaos Cloth workflows, from resizing outfits to fixing collision issues. Check them out.  


**Artist Credit**  
We’d like to extend a special thanks to the artists whose works we’ve shared in the webinar or in this resource list. Make sure to check out [_@aschno Anna Liedtke_](https://www.instagram.com/aschno/), [_Riola_](https://www.instagram.com/reve.riola/), [_Blockschmidt_](https://www.instagram.com/blockschmidt/), [_Vesna Stawa | Orchidea3D_](https://www.instagram.com/orchidea3d/), and[ _Matt Workman_](https://www.instagram.com/cinematographydb/).

content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide and resources for creating, customizing, and integrating MetaHuman garments using CLO, Marvelous Designer, and Unreal Engine workflows.

title: Where Fabric Meets Technology
content:
![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202604/4cddc4b1471b4d46bdba481be3c486a7/images/55371817947549fa83162234f1817683fabr1.PNG)Digital fabric is redefining how we design, develop, and communicate in the apparel industry.

From realistic textures to accurate drape and behavior, digital fabrics allow designers and developers to visualize materials long before physical samples exist. This not only speeds up the product development cycle but also reduces costs, material waste, and the need for multiple sampling rounds.  
![353f48bb610f4d4cadc1fddf8765a26c](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202604/4cddc4b1471b4d46bdba481be3c486a7/images/353f48bb610f4d4cadc1fddf8765a26c1.png)With the rise of 3D design tools, digital fabric libraries are becoming essential assets enabling teams across design, merchandising, and production to collaborate seamlessly with a single source of truth.

Beyond efficiency, digital fabrics open doors to innovation. Designers can experiment freely with colors, patterns, and finishes without limitations, pushing creativity further while staying sustainable.

In a fast-moving industry, digital fabric is no longer optional, it’s a key driver of smarter, faster and more responsible fashion development
content_description: This webpage showcases how digital fabric technology transforms apparel design and production by enhancing creativity, collaboration, and sustainability through realistic 3D visualization and efficient workflows.

title: Error when drag the clothes into metahuman
content:
![479a4e86019a41babb9c862b979e6b21](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202604/ddba1f25eeb647f48ad3060e7d885805/images/479a4e86019a41babb9c862b979e6b21error.png)I followed a tutorial video for CLO on YouTube named "**How to use MetaHumans in CLO"**. At the final step, when I tried to drag the clothes onto the MetaHuman, I got an error message like the one shown in the image. Could anyone explain why this happens and how to fix it?

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: The contents of the error appear to be a Pipeline problem.Please check whether Pipeline is set in the Metahuman Wardrobe Item file as shown in the image below.In addition, it is also recommended to review whether all the processes have been done in order. All files must be linked in the order below before they are set to Metahuman Wardrobe Item.1. Static Mesh2. Skeletal Mesh3. OutfitAsset4. ChaosClothAsset5. Metahuman Wardrobe ItemFor other images, I am attaching it so that you can check BluePrint additionally.Since I'm using the Korean version, there may be some parts that are difficult to see. The expression '스켈레탈 메시' is 'Skeletal Mesh'.For other images, I am attaching it so that you can check BluePrint additionally.Since I'm using the Korean version, there may be some parts that are difficult to see. The expression 'Skeletal Mesh' is 'Skeletal Mesh'.Please run the Sketal Mesh, OutfitAsset, and ChaosClothAsset files to see if the status of the BluePrint Node on the screen is completed well.I hope you have a good result.
Reply 1: thank you so much. Your answer was very helpful. I followed your instructions and no longer see the error message.
Reply 2: I’m having another issue. The clothing looks transparent, even though I didn’t use any opacity map. I checked both the Cloth Asset and the static mesh, and they’re also transparent. I’m not sure why—could you help me figure it out? Thank you very much.
Reply 3: First of all, I think we need to check if the fabric contains an opacity map.You can check it in CLO, but you can also fix it by deleting Opacity Map from Material Blueprint in Unreal Engine.The black mark on the top part of the sleeve is the inside part exposed to the outside during the CLO simulation process. Or, You can definitely complete the simulation in CLO or change the Editor mode of the Unreal Engine to modeling mode and solve it with Dform->sculpting.
Reply 4: I didn't use the opacity map in CLO file. How can I find the Material Blueprint in this window? I don't see any tool to fix it 😭
Reply 5: Material blue print can be found in the material entry in the cloth static mesh file.I checked it on my phone and couldn't see it closely, but I think it would be good to check 'both sides' in the detail of the material. In the new photo you sent me in the comments, the data related to the thickness of the costume is seen in a translucent state.
Reply 6: Thank you so much for your support. I spent many hours trying to fix it, and it seems to have worked quite well. The fabric now looks better and is no longer transparent like before. :D
Reply 7: That's great, and I hope you complete the wonderful results!👍🏻

Comment 2: Hi Mila Dao,I'll have a look and get back to you in the coming days. I'll also investigate the other issue you shared: https://connect.clo-set.com/community/post/ddba1f25eeb647f48ad3060e7d885805 regards,Bryan
Reply 1: Thank you a lot, I await your reply

title: Strange Black Artifacts Appearing in Render (But Not in 3D Viewport)
content:
Hi everyone,

As shown in the attached images, the first image is from the 3D viewport, and the second one is the final rendered result. I have no idea what these messy black lines are in the rendered image.

I’ve tried rendering multiple times from different angles, but those black artifacts still appear consistently. They don’t show up in the 3D window at all.

Does anyone know what might be causing this issue and how I can fix or adjust it?

Thanks in advance!

![ab949130fd5f4b8196a7a1d94b82bb93](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202604/00db2edc2c9541d4b541208eec603a0e/images/ab949130fd5f4b8196a7a1d94b82bb93Screenshot%202026-04-21%20002352.png)![e0cb7753550f4ea2acaaa82a4d3f61f9](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202604/00db2edc2c9541d4b541208eec603a0e/images/e0cb7753550f4ea2acaaa82a4d3f61f9Screenshot%202026-04-21%20002458.png)

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Hi. This can be caused by a few things.Can you please share your Render Settings as well as your fabric properties?Can you also let us know what version of CLO you are currently using since we cannot find your active account in our system to check. Thank you :)
Reply 1: Hi, thanks for getting back to me!I’m currently using the latest version of CLO. However, the issue is a bit confusing, the black lines only show up in the final rendered image. In both the 3D viewport and the Render tab preview, everything looks completely fine.
Reply 2: You are very welcome!A few things. -For Render Engine it looks like you are on a PC, so double check your engine is set to GPU and not CPU-Check your noise setting is not too low. We recommend not going below 0.030-For the Velvet fabric delete the Displacement MapOn a side note we are curious if you used the new lacing feature. They look great!😍
Reply 3: Hi Ariel,It’s working fine now. The render is clean and the black lines are completely gone. Thank you so much for your help!I believe the issue was caused by the displacement map.Also, the new lacing feature is absolutely amazing! I had to try it right away when it launched in the new version because I struggled a lot with lacing before 😄

title: Custom parametric patterns in Pattern Drafter — user-defined parameters and formulas?
content:
Following up on this thread (<https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/community/posts/4407569721753-Parametric-pattern-drafting>)after the Pattern Drafter developments through CLO 2025.0, 2025.2, and 2026.0. The direction so far has been toward AI/image-based pattern generation and more built-in garment types (trousers, skirts), which is welcome. But the original question in this thread about user-defined parametric patterns still seems open.

Two specific questions:

  1. Can I define my own parameters and derived formulas in Pattern Drafter (e.g. param_a = param_b / 2 + constant), or am I limited to the measurement fields CLO exposes for the built-in garment types?

  2. Is there a way to create custom parametric templates beyond the stock types?




If these aren't supported today, is anything planned?

Thanks.

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Hi Daniel, it is currently not possible to define your own parameters. The feature is under constant development and additions will be made in the future, but unfortunately, we cannot give details yet - we'll add your feedback to the request pool, thank you! 🙂
Reply 1: Thanks Melody. Would be really cool to see some more advanced CAD like features in CLO3D. Happy to help with providing input or testing 🙂
content_description: This page explores user capabilities and future plans for custom parametric pattern creation and user-defined formulas within CLO's Pattern Drafter tool.

title: 【画面控制】疑问求解答
content:
clo按住滚动鼠标怎么托动不了怎么办，请问如何解决？  
电脑是MAC BOOK PRO,鼠标是PHILIPS MX prime 4  
  
英语 English

In CLO software, I cannot drag the view by holding down the mouse scroll wheel. How to fix this problem?

My device is a MacBook Pro, and my mouse model is Philips MX Prime 4.

## 韩语 한국어

CLO 프로그램에서 마우스 휠을 누른 채 화면 드래그가 되지 않습니다. 해결 방법을 알려주세요.

사용 기기는 맥북 프로(MacBook Pro)이며, 마우스 모델은 필립스 MX Prime 4입니다.

## 日语 日本語

CLO ソフトでマウスホイールを押しながら画面をドラッグできません。解決方法を教えてください。

使用機器は MacBook Pro、マウス機種はフィリップス MX Prime 4 です。

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Hi There. Have you checked your mouse settings?They can be found under Settings > User Settings > View Control. Then a drop down in the upper right corner. For your mouse you should make sure Regular Mouse is selectedAlso attaching an image for reference
Reply 1: omg，thank you ！！！😭❤️😭❤️
Reply 2: You are very welcome! 🙂
content_description: This webpage provides troubleshooting solutions for resolving the issue of dragging the view in CLO software using the mouse scroll wheel on a MacBook Pro with a Philips MX Prime 4 mouse.
